title: Contraception: method choice, medical eligibility and emergency contraception
subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
setting: Primary care, outpatient, sexual health clinic
summary: Offer all methods, highlighting long-acting reversible contraception (implant, IUDs) as most effective; check every method against WHO MEC or UKMEC 2025 (category 4 = do not use). For emergency contraception offer a copper IUD first, otherwise ulipristal 30 mg up to 120 hours or levonorgestrel 1.5 mg up to 72 hours.

sections.title: Assess and apply MEC categories
items: History: age, parity, postpartum and breastfeeding status, smoking, BMI, blood pressure, migraine type (aura or not), personal or family VTE, cardiovascular disease, cancers, liver and kidney disease, current medicines (enzyme inducers, antiretrovirals) and pregnancy plans.

MEC categories (WHO and UKMEC): 1 no restriction; 2 benefits generally outweigh risks; 3 risks usually outweigh benefits, use only with expert judgement when no acceptable alternative; 4 unacceptable health risk, do not use.
Several category 2 conditions can add up, and several category 3 conditions together may amount to an unacceptable risk (UKMEC 2025).
Measure blood pressure and BMI before combined hormonal contraception (CHC). Routine thrombophilia screening is not appropriate (WHO MEC).
Start a method only when reasonably sure she is not pregnant. A urine pregnancy test cannot exclude pregnancy from sex in the last 21 days, so repeat it 21 days after the last unprotected sex.

sections.title: Method choice and starting
items: Most effective: implant, LNG-IUD and copper IUD (not user-dependent); then DMPA; then CHC and progestogen-only pill (POP), which depend on correct daily use. Only condoms also protect against STIs.

When oestrogen is contraindicated, the copper IUD and progestogen-only methods are usually MEC 1 or 2, but check each condition: DMPA is UKMEC 3 with past VTE, multiple cardiovascular risk factors or vascular disease.

Quick start: no extra precautions if started on days 1 to 5 of a natural cycle (days 1 to 7 for the LNG-IUD). Otherwise use condoms or abstain for 7 days (CHC, implant, DMPA, LNG-IUD) or 2 days (POP). The copper IUD works immediately.

Age: CHC is UKMEC 1 under 40 and 2 from 40 to 50 (not rated beyond 50); DMPA is UKMEC 2 under 18 and over 45 because of bone density; IUDs are UKMEC 2 under 20. Offer all methods, including LARC, to young people.
Prefer a CHC containing levonorgestrel or norethisterone (lowest VTE risk among COCs). Extended or tailored regimens with fewer hormone-free intervals are acceptable.

sections.title: Combined hormonal contraception: category 4 (do not use)
items: Age 35 or over and smoking 15 or more cigarettes a day. Under 15 a day, or stopped less than 1 year ago, is UKMEC 3 (WHO 3 for under 15 a day).
Migraine with aura at any age. Aura only 5 or more years ago is UKMEC 3; migraine without aura is UKMEC 2 to start.
Blood pressure 160/100 mmHg or higher (clinic) or vascular disease. Stage 1 hypertension (140 to 159/90 to 99 mmHg) and controlled hypertension are category 3.
Current or past VTE, known thrombogenic mutation, positive antiphospholipid antibodies (including SLE), major surgery with prolonged immobilisation, or multiple VTE risk factors.
Ischaemic heart disease, stroke or TIA, atrial fibrillation, complicated valvular heart disease, cardiomyopathy with impaired function.
Postpartum under 3 weeks with other VTE risk factors, and breastfeeding under 6 weeks postpartum.
Current breast cancer, decompensated cirrhosis, hepatocellular adenoma or carcinoma, and (UKMEC 2025) nephrotic syndrome or dialysis. BRCA carriers and BMI 35 kg/m2 or more are UKMEC 3.

sections.title: IUD and progestogen-only cautions
items: Do not insert a copper IUD or LNG-IUD (category 4) with pregnancy, current PID, chlamydia, gonorrhoea or Mycoplasma genitalium with clinical signs, or postpartum or post-abortion sepsis.

Also category 4 to insert an IUD: unexplained vaginal bleeding before evaluation, cervical or endometrial cancer awaiting treatment, pelvic TB, and persistently raised hCG or malignant trophoblastic disease.
A distorted uterine cavity (fibroids or anomaly) is UKMEC 3 for IUDs. Insert postpartum within 48 hours or from 4 weeks; insertion between 48 hours and 4 weeks is category 3.
Current breast cancer is category 4 for every hormonal method (past breast cancer category 3); the copper IUD stays category 1.

UKMEC 2025 rates DMPA category 3 with known thrombogenic mutations, positive antiphospholipid antibodies, multiple VTE risk factors, postpartum with other VTE risk factors, and nephrotic syndrome or dialysis (because of a small VTE signal and bone effects).
Enzyme-inducing drugs (rifampicin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, St John's wort, some antiretrovirals) reduce the effect of CHC, POP and implant; prefer an IUD or DMPA and check an interaction checker.

sections.title: Emergency contraception (EC)
items: Offer EC after unprotected sex or method failure (missed pills, late injection, condom failure). Oral EC does not cover sex later in the same cycle; oral EC taken after ovulation is ineffective.

Copper IUD is the most effective EC: insert within 5 days (120 hours) of the first unprotected sex in the cycle, or up to 5 days after the earliest likely ovulation, whichever is later. It then gives ongoing contraception.
Ulipristal acetate 30 mg orally once, as soon as possible and within 120 hours. It is more effective than levonorgestrel and is the oral choice for sex 96 to 120 hours ago or close to ovulation.

Levonorgestrel 1.5 mg orally once, licensed within 72 hours and likely ineffective after 96 hours. Give 3 mg with an enzyme-inducing drug (used now or in the last 28 days; ulipristal not recommended then) and consider 3 mg if BMI above 26 kg/m2 or weight above 70 kg.

After levonorgestrel, quick start hormonal contraception the same day. After ulipristal, wait 5 days before any progestogen-containing method (it can make ulipristal fail), using condoms or abstinence until the new method is effective.
EC can be repeated within a cycle. Do not give levonorgestrel within 5 days after ulipristal; ulipristal may be less effective within 7 days after levonorgestrel or other progestogen.
Pregnancy test 21 days after the last unprotected sex, or sooner if the next period is more than 7 days late, unusually light or painful.

sections.title: Special situations
items: Postpartum: POP and implant can start at any time (UKMEC 1; WHO 2025 rates progestogen-only methods category 2 while breastfeeding under 6 weeks). Avoid CHC for 6 weeks if breastfeeding (then WHO 3 until 6 months, UKMEC 2), and for 3 weeks if not (6 weeks with other VTE risk factors).

Breastfeeding after EC: FSRH (April 2026 amendment) says no interruption is needed after a single ulipristal dose; WHO MEC advises expressing and discarding milk for 1 week. Levonorgestrel has no known adverse effect on breastfeeding.
After sexual assault offer all EC options including the copper IUD (WHO rates IUD insertion category 3 when STI risk is high), plus STI and HIV post-exposure assessment.
UKMEC 2025: prioritise alternatives to CHC in sickle cell trait, chronic kidney disease and e-cigarette users; anxiety and mood disorders no longer carry categories but mood should be monitored.

India: the national programme supplies COC, POP, DMPA, copper IUDs and centchroman (ormeloxifene), a non-steroidal pill taken twice weekly for 3 months then weekly, which WHO MEC does not cover; eligibility for hormonal and intrauterine methods follows WHO MEC.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Prescribing CHC without checking blood pressure, smoking, age and migraine type; migraine with aura is an absolute contraindication.
Giving levonorgestrel when unprotected sex was 96 to 120 hours ago or near ovulation, when a copper IUD or ulipristal would work.
Starting a progestogen method straight after ulipristal, or forgetting enzyme inducers taken in the last 28 days.
Relying on a negative pregnancy test within 21 days of unprotected sex.

drugs.name: Ulipristal acetate (EC)
drugs.dose: 30 mg orally, single dose, as soon as possible within 120 hours of unprotected sex
drugs.notes: Wait 5 days before starting hormonal contraception. Not recommended with enzyme inducers or severe asthma on oral steroids. May be less effective if BMI above 30 kg/m2; do not double the dose.

drugs.name: Levonorgestrel (EC)
drugs.dose: 1.5 mg orally, single dose, within 72 hours (ineffective beyond 96 hours)
drugs.notes: 3 mg with enzyme inducers; consider 3 mg if BMI above 26 kg/m2 or weight above 70 kg. Quick start ongoing contraception the same day.

drugs.name: Copper IUD (EC and ongoing)
drugs.dose: Insert within 120 hours of the first unprotected sex in the cycle, or within 5 days of the earliest likely ovulation
drugs.notes: Most effective EC; unaffected by weight or enzyme inducers. Same contraindications as routine IUD insertion.

drugs.name: Combined oral contraceptive
drugs.dose: Ethinylestradiol 30 micrograms with levonorgestrel 150 micrograms orally daily for 21 days then a 7-day break, or a tailored or continuous regimen
drugs.notes: Check MEC first. 7 days of extra precautions unless started on days 1 to 5.

drugs.name: Desogestrel progestogen-only pill
drugs.dose: 75 micrograms orally once daily without a break
drugs.notes: 12-hour missed-pill window. 2 days of extra precautions unless started on days 1 to 5.

drugs.name: Medroxyprogesterone acetate (DMPA)
drugs.dose: 150 mg deep IM (or 104 mg subcutaneously) every 13 weeks
drugs.notes: Bone density loss and delayed return of fertility; UKMEC 2 under 18 and over 45. 7 days of extra precautions unless given on days 1 to 5.

drugs.name: Etonogestrel implant
drugs.dose: 68 mg subdermal implant in the inner upper arm, replace every 3 years
drugs.notes: Irregular bleeding is the main side effect. Reduced by enzyme inducers.
